to do (to perform or execute an action)
to do (harm or good, but negative by default)

My husband has done me so much good.

to put, to place, to add (especially of smaller objects or ingredients)
Ich würde noch was Salz an die Kartoffeln tun.
I'd add some more salt to the potatoes.
to make a difference; to be different
Does that make much of a difference?
Die beiden Kameras tun sich nichts.
The two cameras are no different [i.e. neither better than the other].
to happen, to be going on (as opposed to a lack of activity)
There's a lot going on at the moment.
Used with the preceding infinitive of another verb that has been fronted to the first position, typically for strong emphasis or contrast with another verb
Er singt immer noch gern, aber tanzen tut er gar nicht mehr.
He still loves singing, but as to dancing, he doesn't do that anymore at all.
Used with the following infinitive of another verb, without fronting, to convey continuousness or general emphasis on an action
I am listening! (as a response to the reproach that one is not)
Ich tu das jetzt mal aufräumen.
Used in the past subjunctive with the infinitive of another verb to form the conditional tense (instead of standard würde)
Ich tät mir das noch mal überlegen.
tun.et: From Middle High German tuon, from Old High German tuon, from Proto-West Germanic *dōn, from Proto-Germanic *dōną, derived from Proto-Indo-European *dʰeh₁- (“to put, set, place”). Cognate with English do.
